prerequisites: Required prior knowledge from the Business course taught in the second year.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the main characteristics of managerial work.
Understand the concept of the management process and its integrated functions.
Determine the relationships between company culture and the exercise of management functions.
Understand the arguments for and against Corporate Social Responsibility, and the main pitfalls it must overcome to be ethical and socially responsible.
Know the phases of a planning process and the orientations it can adopt.
Be able to apply the main strategic analysis and diagnostic tools.
Be able to apply the implications of motivational and leadership theories to managerial action.
Understand the concept of control and its interrelationship with other management functions.
Produce a grammatically correct, well-structured, clear, content-rich written text, appropriate for the communicative situation.
Organize and participate in work teams, fostering aptitudes for empathy, negotiation, and optimization of time and affected personnel.
Effectively present and explain individually or group-produced work in a debate environment to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

syllabus_topics: Theme 1. Introduction. Global vision of the company
Concept of ownership and management: entrepreneur and manager
The work of management: leadership styles
Planning process and types of planning
The process of objective setting and decision making
From strategic planning to strategic management
The parts of the organization: Formal and informal organization
Definition of control function and phases of the control process
Types of control in the company
teaching_methods: Cooperative Learning (CoopLearning) methodology, based on cooperative learning, critical thinking, and real-world business challenges.
Expository class: Participatory lecture, conferences, company visits, fair attendance.
Participatory class: Individual or group case resolution, role-playing, technical application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates.
Integrated project: Project work involving planning, design, and execution of activities to solve a problem or task.
Tutoring: Personalized and small group attention, review of class materials, learning guidance, work completion, student consultations, scheduled tutorials.
Group work: Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects.
Individual study: Preparation of readings, exams, exercises, class preparation.

assessment_methods.method: Individual written knowledge tests (objective tests, development, short answers, problems, comments, evaluations, etc.)
Written tests through reports/memoirs and presentation of team and individual work on specific course content
Business Project - Integrated Project (oral presentation and defense)

assessment_rules: For the first call, the final grade consists of 50% from the Integrated Business Project (including oral presentation), 20% from academic work and class participation, and 30% from a final knowledge test. A minimum score of 40% is required on the final knowledge test to pass the course. For the second call, students can choose between two options: Option 1 allows retaining grades from the integrated project (max 25%) and continuous assessment (max 30%), with a knowledge test making up max 45%, requiring a minimum of 40% on the written test. Option 2 allows students to renounce previous grades, with the knowledge test constituting up to 100% of the final grade.
